title: The cohomology of the I^nF is a finite module over the Rees algebra
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $B=\mathcal R_A(I)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^nt^n\subseteq A[t]$ the Rees algebra of $I$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra] (the subring of $A[t]$ of the polynomials whose coefficient of $t^n$ lies in $I^n$ for every $n$), $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to f^*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $\mathcal I^0\mathcal F=\mathcal F$ and, for $n\ge1$, let $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F\subseteq\mathcal F$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0). Fix $q\ge0$ and write $M_n=H^q(X,\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)$ for $n\ge0$ (sheaf cohomology [pqf-def-cohomology]; an $A$-module, $a\in A$ acting through its image $f^\sharp(a)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$). For $k,m\ge0$ and $a\in I^k$, multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ maps $\mathcal I^m\mathcal F$ into $\mathcal I^{m+k}\mathcal F$ (on every open $U$, $f^\sharp(a)|_U$ is a section of $\mathcal I^k$); let $\lambda^{(m)}_a:\mathcal I^m\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^{m+k}\mathcal F$ be this $\mathcal O_X$-linear map and, for $x\in M_m$, put $a\star x=H^q(X,\lambda^{(m)}_a)(x)\in M_{m+k}$. Then: (1) $M=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}M_n$ is a $B$-module under $\big(\sum_ka_kt^k\big)\cdot(x_m)_{m\ge0}=\big(\sum_{k+m=n}a_k\star x_m\big)_{n\ge0}$ ($a_k\in I^k$, $x_m\in M_m$, almost all zero), and for $a\in A=I^0$ and $x\in M_m$ the element $a\star x$ is the product $ax$ of the $A$-module structure of $M_m$; (2) $M$ is a finitely generated $B$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02O8 (lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F, line 5380; reference EGA III Cor 3.3.2) and the paragraph before it (lines 5370-5376), which gives M = (+)_n H^p(X, I^n F) its structure of graded S = (+)_n I^n-module; Stacks' proof applies Lemma 0897 (lemma-graded-finiteness) part (1) to the finite type graded f^*B~-module (+)_n I^n F. Stacks writes I^nF for the image of f^*(I^n)~ (x) F -> F, which equals (I O_X)^n F as used here. Tags verified in tags/tags: 02O8, 0897.

proof.text: (The sheaves $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ and the maps $\lambda_a$.) $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is covered by the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Noetherian, so it is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and it is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (iii), hence a Noetherian scheme; $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], in particular locally Noetherian, and the coherent $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. $\widetilde I$ is a quasi-coherent ideal of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$ with $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\widetilde I)=I$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (the localization at the powers of $1$), so by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1) (with $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A=V$, $\mathcal J=\widetilde I$) $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ is a quasi-coherent ideal and $\mathcal I(U)=f^\sharp(I)\mathcal O_X(U)$ for every affine open $U\subseteq X$ (writing $f^\sharp(a)$ also for its restriction to $U$). By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1), (2), applied to $\mathcal J=\mathcal I$ and then to $\mathcal J=\mathcal I^n$ (quasi-coherent by (1)), every $\mathcal I^n$ is a quasi-coherent ideal, every $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, and for affine $U$ with $C=\mathcal O_X(U)$: $\mathcal I^n(U)=\mathcal I(U)^n=(f^\sharp(I)C)^n=f^\sharp(I^n)C$ and $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)(U)=f^\sharp(I^n)\,\mathcal F(U)$, the $C$-submodule generated by the $f^\sharp(a)s$, $a\in I^n$, $s\in\mathcal F(U)$ (also for $n=0$, $\mathcal I^0\mathcal F=\mathcal F$). Now let $k,m\ge0$, $a\in I^k$, $V\subseteq X$ open and $s\in(\mathcal I^m\mathcal F)(V)$. Every point of $V$ has an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq V$ (affine opens form a basis of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]), and there $s|_U=\sum_jf^\sharp(a_j)u_j$ with $a_j\in I^m$, $u_j\in\mathcal F(U)$, so $f^\sharp(a)s|_U=\sum_jf^\sharp(aa_j)u_j\in f^\sharp(I^{m+k})\mathcal F(U)=(\mathcal I^{m+k}\mathcal F)(U)$; since $\mathcal I^{m+k}\mathcal F$ is a subsheaf of $\mathcal F$, $f^\sharp(a)s\in(\mathcal I^{m+k}\mathcal F)(V)$. So multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ gives the $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\lambda^{(m)}_a:\mathcal I^m\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^{m+k}\mathcal F$ of the statement (the first assertion in the statement's definition of $\star$), and directly from this description: $\lambda^{(m)}_{a+a'}=\lambda^{(m)}_a+\lambda^{(m)}_{a'}$ for $a,a'\in I^k$ ($f^\sharp$ additive); $\lambda^{(m+l)}_a\circ\lambda^{(m)}_{a'}=\lambda^{(m)}_{aa'}$ for $a\in I^k$, $a'\in I^l$ ($f^\sharp(a)f^\sharp(a')=f^\sharp(aa')$, $aa'\in I^{k+l}$); and for $a\in A=I^0$, $\lambda^{(m)}_a$ is multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ on $\mathcal I^m\mathcal F$.

proof.text: (The Rees algebra as a graded algebra of finite type.) $B=\mathcal R_A(I)$ [def-nagata-rees-algebra] is a commutative subring of $A[t]$, graded by $B_k=I^kt^k$ [prop-nagata-rees-graded], with $B_kB_l\subseteq B_{k+l}$ ($(at^k)(a't^l)=aa't^{k+l}$, $aa'\in I^{k+l}$); $B_0=I^0t^0\cong A$ by the constant coefficient [lemma-nagata-rees-degree-zero], and $B$ is an $A$-algebra through $a\mapsto a\,t^0=a\cdot1\in B_0$. As $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I=(x_0,\dots,x_r)$ for finitely many $x_i\in A$ (if $I=0$ take $r=0$, $x_0=0$), so $B$ is generated as an algebra over $B_0=A$ by $x_0t,\dots,x_rt$ [prop-nagata-rees-finite-generation]; hence the $A$-algebra map $A[y_0,\dots,y_r]\to B$, $y_i\mapsto x_it$, is surjective and $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra].

source.place: Lemma 02O8, proof: B = (+)_n I^n is the graded A-algebra to which Lemma 0897 is applied (finitely generated since A is Noetherian)

proof.text: (The graded data over $B$.) Put $\mathcal G_m=\mathcal I^m\mathcal F$ ($m\ge0$), quasi-coherent by step 1, and for $b=at^k\in B_k$ ($a\in I^k$; $a$ is determined by $b$) put $\mu^{(m)}_b=\lambda^{(m)}_a:\mathcal G_m\to\mathcal G_{m+k}$ (step 1). The identities of step 1 are conditions (i), (ii), (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-graded-finiteness-cohomology]: (i) $at^k+a't^k=(a+a')t^k$; (ii) $(at^k)(a't^l)=aa't^{k+l}$ (step 2); (iii) $a\cdot1=at^0$ and $\lambda^{(m)}_a$ is multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ for $a\in A$. For condition (iv): $\mathcal F$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], so $X$ is covered by opens $U$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F|_U$; let $s_1,\dots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)=\mathcal G_0(U)$ be the images of the basis sections and $d_i=0$. Let $m\ge0$, $V\subseteq U$ open, $t\in\mathcal G_m(V)$ and $x\in V$. Choose an affine open $x\in U'\subseteq V$ [def-pc-scheme]; by step 1, $t|_{U'}=\sum_jf^\sharp(a_j)u_j$ with $a_j\in I^m$, $u_j\in\mathcal F(U')$. By surjectivity of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}\to\mathcal F|_U$ there is an open $x\in W\subseteq U'$ with $u_j|_W=\sum_ic_{ij}s_i|_W$, $c_{ij}\in\mathcal O_X(W)$, for all $j$. Then $t|_W=\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}f^\sharp(a_j)s_i|_W=\sum_i\sum_jc_{ij}\,\mu^{(0)}_{a_jt^m}(s_i)|_W$ with $a_jt^m\in B_{m-0}$, which is (iv).

source.place: Lemma 02O8, proof: 'Since B surjects onto (+) I^n O_X it is clear that (+) I^n F is a finite type graded B-module'

proof.text: (Conclusion: (1) and (2).) By steps 2 and 3 the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-graded-finiteness-cohomology] hold for $A$, $B=\mathcal R_A(I)$, $f$, $(\mathcal G_m)=(\mathcal I^m\mathcal F)$, the maps $\mu$ and $p=q$. Its $M_m=H^q(X,\mathcal I^m\mathcal F)$ is our $M_m$, and for $b_k=a_kt^k$ ($a_k\in I^k$) and $x_m\in M_m$ its product $H^q(X,\mu^{(m)}_{b_k})(x_m)=H^q(X,\lambda^{(m)}_{a_k})(x_m)=a_k\star x_m$ [pqf-def-cohomology]. So its conclusion says that $M=\bigoplus_nM_n$ is a $B$-module under $\big(\sum_ka_kt^k\big)\cdot(x_m)_m=\big(\sum_{k+m=n}a_k\star x_m\big)_n$, which is the first assertion of (1), and that $M$ is a finitely generated $B$-module, which is (2). For the last assertion of (1): for $a\in A=I^0$ and $x\in M_m$, $a\star x=H^q(X,\lambda^{(m)}_a)(x)$, and $\lambda^{(m)}_a$ is multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$ on $\mathcal I^m\mathcal F$ (step 1); by the convention of the statement ($a\in A$ acts on $M_m=H^q(X,\mathcal I^m\mathcal F)$ through $f^\sharp(a)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, i.e. as $H^q$ of multiplication by $f^\sharp(a)$) this is $ax$.
